system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
The Seller’s **[STANDARD] labels and “reviewer efficiency note” are not evidence of Buyer agreement**. All positions require review. The Buyer targets below are proposed negotiating positions, not agreed terms.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What the Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | A materially higher general cap, with separate treatment for fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities and fraud. | **Counter at 50% / AUD 12m**, subject to diligence and available security for claims—20% leaves substantial acquisition risk with Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000**; **AUD 250,000 deductible basket**, recovering only the excess. | Lower thresholds; related claims aggregated; a tipping basket; exclusions for separately protected categories. | **Propose AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 100,000 tipping basket**, with related claims treated together—otherwise recurring smaller losses may be unrecoverable. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | General warranty notice within **18 months**; limitations extend to all Claims unless excluded. | At least **24 months** for general warranties, workable notice requirements and separate category-specific periods. | **Seek 24 months and reject blanket extension to all Claims**—Buyer needs sufficient operating and reporting cycles to identify problems. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title subject to the general cap and time limit. | Separate protection for capacity, ownership, valid issue and unencumbered transfer of all shares; no basket or de minimis. | **Require at least a 100% price cap and a materially longer period, proposed at seven years**, subject to applicable law—defective ownership undermines the entire acquisition. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | No express fraud protection identified; limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance apply to all Claims. | Express preservation of fraud and fraudulent misrepresentation claims, including appropriate attribution of Seller representatives’ conduct. | **Exclude fraud expressly from caps, thresholds, contractual time bars, disclosure/knowledge defences and remedy restrictions**—Seller must not contractually shelter fraudulent conduct. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the data room, referenced material, accounts, registers and public records. | Only sufficiently detailed, fair disclosure enabling Buyer to understand the nature and scope of the relevant matter; a frozen, accessible disclosure record. | **Reject blanket deemed disclosure; require specific warranty-linked disclosures and an agreed data-room snapshot**—document availability alone should not transfer unidentified risks to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | Bars claims for Buyer/adviser knowledge, including anything discoverable from data-room or public records. | Preferably no knowledge bar; fallback limited to actual conscious knowledge of named Buyer personnel, without constructive or imputed adviser knowledge. | **Delete “discoverable” and adviser-imputation wording; preserve specific indemnities regardless of knowledge**—diligence access should not substitute for Seller warranties. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied upon delivery of written consent. No final consent or evidence of satisfied conditions disclosed. | A Buyer-waivable completion condition requiring valid consent and satisfaction of relevant clause 11.3 conditions, without materially adverse changes. | **Do not complete until effective consent and associated conditions are evidenced**—approximately 30% of FY26 revenue is exposed. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** remains outstanding; security release follows Completion. | Verified payout figures, repayment through completion funds flow and effective releases of security and relevant guarantees at Completion. | **Require coordinated repayment and discharge at Completion, with debt deducted under the agreed price mechanics**—post-completion release leaves Buyer exposed and conflicts with a debt-free acquisition. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional completion bonuses described as Seller’s matter but omitted from funds flow; on-costs unspecified. | Seller bears transaction-triggered bonuses and applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs; accurate payment and accounting treatment. | **Quantify and include these amounts as Seller-funded payments or an appropriate price deduction, without double counting**—otherwise Buyer may inherit an unfunded completion liability. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; **AUD 180,000** recorded open, with no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment. | Verified payment and effective IP transfer by Completion, plus protection against pre-completion ownership defects, claims and reasonable remediation costs. | **Require cleared-payment evidence and a confirmatory assignment, backed by a broader standalone indemnity**—paying a fee alone may not establish or remedy complete IP ownership. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary operational issue, said unlikely to be material; access, scope and notification requirements remain unresolved. | Prompt investigation, evidence preservation, containment and an assessment of legal notification obligations; targeted protection for pre-completion incident consequences. | **Require investigation milestones, reporting/cooperation covenants and a specific indemnity for resulting liabilities and reasonable response costs**—uncertainty warrants protection, not an assumption of either no incident or a confirmed notifiable breach. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals of **AUD 110,000 each / AUD 330,000 total** characterised as ordinary-course costs. | Verification of aggregate commitments, timing, termination rights, accruals and whether renewals are genuinely ordinary course. | **Review DD-008 and DD-011 together; require Buyer approval for material new commitments and allocate costs according to their substance**—neither “ordinary course” nor debt-like treatment is established by the disclosure. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | General limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance extend across all Claims unless expressly excluded. | Distinct regimes for general warranties, fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities, payment/price obligations and fraud. | **Rewrite the limitations using an express category-by-category application matrix**—otherwise blanket provisions can defeat specifically negotiated protections. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Relies on DD-012 share register showing Seller holds 100%. | Independent verification of the complete issued capital, ownership chain, encumbrances, options and other rights, plus proper transfer deliverables. | **Reconcile registers with corporate records and supporting issue/transfer documents; obtain searches, releases and fundamental warranties**—the register is important evidence, not a complete title investigation. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP treated as settled within the general regime. | Separate pre-completion tax protection with an appropriately longer claims period; robust IP ownership, licensing and infringement protection beyond Ironquay. | **Reopen both: seek a standalone tax indemnity and tailored tax period, plus separately negotiated IP scope, cap and survival**—their exposure and discovery periods are not adequately addressed by the general package. |

**Completion priorities:** effective Bluefen consent, Riverlark repayment/releases, funded bonus treatment, Ironquay ownership evidence and verified share title. Unresolved risks should be addressed expressly through completion conditions, price treatment, indemnities and, where appropriate, escrow or retention—not merely disclosed away.
=== END ADVICE ===
